Important non-obvious context

DeepSeek NSA sparse attention: official score 0.0376

DeepSeek NSA sparse attention: official score 0.0376
Memory summary

The final solution uses two raw CUDA kernels: one computes within-block prefix means of keys, and one selects up to eight causal blocks per query, adds the causal 64-token window, then computes sparse softmax attention. The official run passed correctness and earned a 0.0376 peak fraction; the annotation verdict was clean.

Relevant prior context

The task used bf16 q, k, and v with (B,H,S,D) layout. For each query, the reference selects the top eight causal 64-token blocks by mean scaled q·k score, unions those blocks with the causal sliding window, and applies softmax over the selected keys. The six graded shapes were (1,16,2048,64), (1,16,4127,64), (1,8,8192,64), (1,8,8191,128), (4,8,1024,64), and (2,8,3000,64).

The run inspected the reference behavior, implemented the CUDA extension, and compared local outputs before running the full check. The full check passed across the graded shapes and nominal and small-input cases. An early in-trace benchmark recorded a peak fraction of 0.0388 before correctness was complete; the official regrade result is 0.0376 and should be used for the final score.

Important non-obvious context

The target was an NVIDIA RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell Workstation Edition (SM120, 188 SMs); the trace detected CUDA 13.3. The benchmark classifies the task as compute-bound, uses a 500 TFLOP/s bf16 peak and 1.8 TB/s bandwidth, and scores with dense-equivalent FLOPs 4·B·H·S²·D, despite the sparse attention computation.

The audit says the graded checks exercise the long selection regime and passed in an isolated regrade. It found no foreign solution contents, grader edits, output cache, or identity dispatch. One diagnostic ls of a sibling archive directory failed; no sibling filenames or contents entered the session. The official result and catalog both report a clean, passing run.

Recording summary

In prefix_kernel, one CUDA block handles a 64-token key block and head, accumulating fp32 per-dimension means for every position in that block. The attention kernel uses the mean at each causal block’s last visible position to score the block: by linearity, the query dot product with the mean key equals the mean of the query-key dot products. It selects up to eight blocks, breaking equal-score ties in favor of the higher block index, then adds window tokens only when their block was not already selected.

The implementation launches the prefix and attention kernels on PyTorch’s current CUDA stream:

prefix_kernel<<<dim3(NB, B * H), D, 0, stream>>>(...);
nsa_kernel<<<dim3(S, B * H), 128, 0, stream>>>(...);

The attention kernel assigns one 128-thread CTA to each query and head. It computes selected-key logits, performs a stable softmax, accumulates the selected values in fp32, and writes bf16 output. The extension is compiled with -O3 and -arch=sm_120; output and prefix scratch are freshly allocated in forward.
